name: Investment Readiness Operating Workflow
description: Deterministic strategic framework to prepare an organization for investor due diligence by orchestrating the creation, validation, organization, publication, and maintenance of an analytics-enabled Investor Data Room.
logic: Investment opportunities are often won or lost during investor due diligence. Even exceptional companies lose investor confidence when information is incomplete, inconsistent, or poorly organized. Build a structured diligence experience that demonstrates operational maturity.
chainsOfThought: Step 1: Assess Investment Readiness -> Evaluate Maturity across Strategy, Finance, Legal, Product, Commercial & Operations -> Calculate Readiness Score & Gap Analysis
Step 2: Coordinate Required Deliverables -> Inventory Executive Summary, Financial Models, Legal Docs & Tech Architecture -> Build Collection Status Dashboard
Step 3: Validate Workflow Dependencies -> Confirm Prerequisite Workflows Completed -> Generate Go/No-Go Recommendation
Step 4: Validate Organizational Knowledge -> Run Document Validation (Accuracy, Evidence, Approvals) -> Audit Claims against Evidence Matrix
Step 5: Organize Institutional Knowledge -> Apply Standardized Folder Taxonomy, Document Naming & Metadata Standards -> Assign Confidentiality Classifications
Step 6: Configure Investor Data Room -> Setup DocSend Space Structure, Navigation Hierarchy, Access Controls & Security Settings
Step 7: Create Investor Experience -> Synthesize Investor Guide, Welcome Message, Diligence Roadmap & Investor FAQ
Step 8: Validate Investor Experience -> Conduct Internal Mock Due Diligence Review -> Confirm Navigation, Accessibility & Story Consistency
Step 9: Publish & Monitor -> Grant Investor Access -> Track Time-On-Document Analytics & Engagement Signals
Step 10: Maintain Investment Readiness -> Maintain Version Control History -> Refresh Financial & Governance Data Continuously
bestPractices: Only approved deliverables are eligible for publication within the Investor Data Room.
Every published document should have one owner, one approved version, and one authoritative location.
Could a first-time investor understand our business within thirty minutes? Can every document be located within two minutes?
Require explicit human executive sign-off before publishing data rooms or sharing materials with investors.
